NL GOVERNMENT ANNOUNCES $500 PAYMENT PER CHILD
(Nov 16th)
The Government of Newfoundland and Labrador has announced a new Family Affordability Benefit, providing a one-time, tax-free payment of $500 per child to eligible families across the province.
Premier Tony Wakeham announced the benefit Monday, which will provide more than $38 million in direct financial support to approximately 46,500 families and 77,000 children throughout Newfoundland and Labrador.
WHO IS ELIGIBLE?
Families receiving the Canada Child Benefit (CCB) with children under the age of 18 will qualify for the payment.
Eligible families will receive:
1 child: $500
2 children: $1,000
3 children: $1,500
4 children: $2,000
WHEN WILL PAYMENTS BE ISSUED?
The Department of Finance will begin issuing payments by cheque before the end of 2026.
Families who are not already receiving the Canada Child Benefit must file their 2025 income tax return and apply for the CCB by December 31st, 2026, to qualify.
The new benefit is part of more than $180 million in recently announced provincial affordability measures, including the $500 Seniors Affordability Payment, increased Home Heating Rebate, electricity rebate and temporary elimination of the provincial gasoline and diesel tax.
According to the Provincial Government, these measures, combined with initiatives announced in Budget 2026, represent more than $380 million in affordability support over the past six months.

MAN ARRESTED FOLLOWING VANDALISM AT RCMP DETACHMENT
(Nov 16th)
A 57-year-old Catalina man is facing three criminal charges following an investigation into a series of deliberate attempts to damage police and private property at the Bonavista RCMP detachment.
The investigation was launched in late October by the RCMP East District General Investigation Section (GIS) and Clarenville-Bonavista District RCMP.
On Sunday, October 25, officers discovered sharp objects believed to have been deliberately placed at the entrance and exit of the detachment’s operational parking lot on Confederation Drive. The objects were positioned in a manner that could damage vehicle tires, potentially affecting police vehicles and privately owned vehicles belonging to employees.
Over the following days, officers made similar discoveries on as many as three additional occasions. At least one police emergency vehicle sustained tire damage as a result of the incidents.
Following an investigation, police identified a suspect and arrested 57-year-old Frederick Anstey of Catalina on November 13, 2026.
Anstey faces three charges under the Criminal Code, including two counts of mischief under $5,000 for interfering with the lawful use or enjoyment of property and one count of mischief under $5,000 for causing damage to property.
He was later released on strict conditions and is scheduled to appear in Clarenville Provincial Court on January 14, 2027.
The investigation remains ongoing, and additional charges are possible.

COLLISION - CORNWALL AVENUE
(Nov 16th)
~ 10:40 a.m; Officers with the Royal Newfoundland Constabulary and NL Health Services paramedics are on the scene of a two-vehicle collision at the intersection of Cornwall Avenue and Craigmilliar Avenue in St. John’s.
Traffic is down to one alternating lane. Please use caution.

HOT TOPIC GRAND OPENING AT AVALON MALL THIS FRIDAY
(Nov 16th)
Shoppers will soon have a new store to visit at Avalon Mall as Hot Topic prepares to celebrate its grand opening this Friday, November 20th.
The store will mark the occasion with giveaways, special offers, and more throughout the weekend, with something planned for each day.
As part of the grand opening celebrations, the first 100 people in line will receive a $30 Hot Topic gift card.
The grand opening takes place this Friday at Avalon Mall.
Avalon Mall.

RNC SEIZE VEHICLE FOLLOWING FAILED ROADSIDE TEST IN CORNER BROOK
(Nov 16th)
A 29-year-old man is without his vehicle after being stopped by the Royal Newfoundland Constabulary (RNC) in Corner Brook Saturday evening.
At approximately 5:45 p.m. on November 14, Operational Patrol Services conducted a traffic safety stop on Main Street.
During the stop, the driver showed signs of impairment and failed a roadside screening test.
As a result, the driver was issued a driving suspension, and his vehicle was seized.
The RNC continues to urge the public to report dangerous or impaired driving directly to police by calling 911.

CONVENIENCE STORE DESTROYED BY FIRE IN APPLETON N.L
(Nov 16th)
First responders were on the scene Sunday morning (November 15th), battling the remnants of a fire that ripped through Renie’s Convenience, located along the Trans-Canada Highway in Appleton, a small community in Central Newfoundland.
The structure was completely destroyed by the fire.
Following the incident, the Glenwood & Appleton Fire Department issued a message thanking the community for its support and recognizing the firefighters who responded to the blaze.
The department also extended its appreciation to Gander Fire Rescue for their assistance during the response.
In its message, the department shared its thoughts with the owners, employees, and everyone affected by the devastating loss.
The department also thanked residents for the overwhelming support shown to firefighters, including donations of food, snacks, and beverages throughout the response.
“Your kindness and generosity did not go unnoticed,” the department stated, adding that the community’s support means more than words can express.
Further details surrounding the incident have not yet been released. More information will be provided as it becomes available.
Karla Sceviour.

FIRE INCIDENT - DONOVAN ST
(November 15th, 2026)
~ 9:10 p.m; An SJRFD Captain confirmed to NFLD Bulletin at the scene that the incident was caused by dryer lint. There was no fire, smoke or damage reported, and no injuries
~ 9:00 p.m; Emergency crews are on scene of a reported fire incident on Donovan Street in Mount Pearl.
The incident appears to be minor in nature, with the majority of fire fighters having since cleared the scene.
SJRFD and RNC remain on scene. More information will be posted as it becomes available.
